items.t: Said Arizonans have the chance in November to protect abortion access rights in the state Constitution and that these rights also need protection at the national level.
items.q: Let’s be very clear: We have the chance this November to protect in our state Constitution our rights to reproductive freedom, but we also have to protect these rights at the national level as well.

items.t: Said she wants Arizona's future generations to inherit a sustainable world.
items.q: As a mother of two small children, I want Arizona's future generations to inherit a sustainable world.

items.t: Said, with Sen. Anna Hernandez, that they were concerned CPAC and other GOP allies would use this ability to harass and intimidate people using ballot drop boxes.
items.q: Sen. Priya Sundareshan and Sen. Anna Hernandez said in a joint statement on Aug. 29 that they are concerned that CPAC and other GOP allies will use this ability to harass and intimidate those using ballot drop boxes.

items.t: Said she knows politics needs more science-based decision-making.
items.q: Having studied engineering at MIT and law and natural resource economics at the U of A, I know we need more science-based decision-making in politics.

record.t: Was elected to the Arizona Senate to represent Legislative District 18.
record.q: Priya Sundareshan was elected to the Arizona Senate in 2023 to represent Legislative District 18.

record.t: Served as Ranking Member on the Senate Elections and Natural Resources/Energy/Water Committees and sat on the Government Committee.
record.q: She is Ranking Member on the Senate Elections and Natural Resources/Energy/Water Committees and also sits on the Government Committee.
